A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiniLM cross-encoder study. All ten pages of v1 and twenty-one pages of v2, including Appendices A–G, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the work and its evidence.

before.justification: V1 reports original patching experiments, head ablations, IDF interventions, and regression and retrieval evaluations in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds activation-patching analyses, unsafe-token editing experiments, and NFCorpus fine-tuning results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The core circuit, path-patching procedure, SVD editing, and SemanticBM formulation remain. Appendix F.2 adds dataset-IDF-aligned initialization followed by full or embedding-only fine-tuning, extending v1's editing procedure and proposed future adaptation.

E1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds an unsafe-token injection scenario using the LDNOOBW lexicon and existing diagnostic samples. The MS MARCO diagnostics and twelve BEIR collections remain; NFCorpus was already included, so its new fine-tuning experiment does not add a dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix F.2 introduces full and embedding-only fine-tuning as comparisons for their IDF-aligned counterparts, with all four conditions displayed in Figure 20. The BM25 and Random Features comparisons in Table 2 are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces substantial new evaluation designs: selecting score-raising unsafe injections, sweeping editing strength, measuring mitigation and nDCG across all ranks, and comparing four fine-tuning conditions using NDCG@1. Existing regression splits and BM25 top-ten candidate retrieval remain. The fine-tuning budget is inconsistent: F.2 states ten epochs, whereas Figure 20 displays thirty.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds activation-patching analysis of shared exact/semantic mechanisms, and C.2 expands upstream Matching Head tracing beyond v1's three selected heads. Appendix F adds editing-strength robustness tests and IDF-alignment/parameter-freezing controls. Existing mean ablation and TFC2/LNC1 analyses are retained, with the latter plots relocated.

E5.justification: V2 reports three random seeds for the new fine-tuning experiment and identifies seed 15 in Figure 20; v1 reports no seed-based repetitions. However, v2 provides no aggregate uncertainty across those seeds. Table 2's existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported patching effects change: head 10.1 has nearly equal TFC/STMC effects in v1 Figure 3 but values of 0.97/0.74 in v2 Figure 2; upstream correlation changes from 1.0 to 0.83. Appendix F adds 80.396% mitigation across 17,537 adversarial samples, nDCG of 0.9861, and fine-tuning curves. The linear-fit correlation of 0.8157 and every Table 2 entry remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SVD decomposition, Matching Score definition, and linear circuit approximation are unchanged. V2 adds the standard BM25 formula as background explanation, without introducing new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central findings remain: a BM25-like circuit, low-rank IDF encoding, and linear reconstruction of cross-encoder scores. V2 additionally makes an explicit first-work claim for causally uncovering an internal neural-IR relevance circuit in Section 2.2.

C2.justification: V2 interprets revised patching effects as possible preference for exact matches and explicitly contrasts query contextualization with BM25's independent term weighting. Its stronger interpretation of BM25-like length normalization includes a decreasing-attention statement in Section 4.3 that contradicts the increasing trend retained in Appendix D/Figure 18. Existing limitations are largely relocated.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code/resource availability link and specifies 2,000 diagnostic pairs for logit/intermediate-head patching and 100 for Matching Head patching. It also documents unsafe-token filtering and new editing/fine-tuning settings. These disclosures do not establish increased sample sizes for retained experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds foundational axiomatic/BM25 citations, Tenney et al.'s NLP-pipeline analogy, and LDNOOBW for the new experiment, while dropping works such as Geiger et al. and Heimersheim/Nanda. Its causal-versus-correlational positioning remains, with a newly explicit first-causal-circuit claim.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, methodology, and circuit explanations are extensively rewritten. Model description moves earlier; detailed path patching, generalization experiments, and holistic axiomatic discussion move to appendices. Limitations are consolidated, and Contextual Query Representation Heads are renamed Query Contextualization Heads.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the circuit overview and attention visualizations, adds extensive patching heatmaps and application Figures 19–20, and relocates the path-patching diagram, TFC2/LNC1 plots, and Table 2 to appendices. Table 2 becomes full-width, alongside substantial page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the causal evidence more inspectable through detailed and broader patching results, adds resource-access information, and tests previously proposed applications. However, its LNC1 summary contradicts the retained result, and fine-tuning documentation specifies ten epochs and three seeds while Figure 20 shows thirty epochs for one seed. With core reconstruction results unchanged, these gains and reporting regressions leave the net quality direction uncertain.
